transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Time: 16:00 UTC (52 minutes)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (HelioBridge Head of Alliances), Eric Wong (HelioBridge Partner Sales Director), Sofia Ramos (HelioBridge Solutions Architect)

---
[00:00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining, we only have about 50 minutes so we'll try to move through the pipeline triage and the technical handoff. quick round — Jordan (redwood) and Priya (redwood) on the call. Maya, Eric, Sofia, do you want to do quick intros?
[00:00:12] Maya Patel: hi all, maya here, head of alliances at HelioBridge. excited to get the technical plan lined up.
[00:00:17] Eric Wong: Eric, partner sales lead, i'll be driving co-sell motions with our field.
[00:00:21] Sofia Ramos: Sofia, solutions architect, i'll own pilots and integrations.
[00:00:25] Jordan Lee: great, thanks. quick agenda: one, map the pilot scope and target accounts; two, walk the technical checklist (SSO, network, data retention); three, pricing/seller SKUs and how we present co-sell offers; four, next steps and owners. sound good?
[00:00:38] Maya Patel: yes.

Summary notes / early clarifications:
[00:01:05] Priya Shah: i pulled together an initial bench plan — it's on the shared drive, benchmark spreadsheet has latency and token cost sims for hosted vs dedicated. note: some of the kernel numbers might be labeled weirdly, i.e. "redwood-dedicated" shows up as "RWD-ded" in the export, so ignore that label if you're scanning. link posted in chat (Helio playbook).
[00:01:36] Sofia Ramos: saw that, thanks. quick question — for the pilot, are we recommending hosted api or dedicated? our customers are price-sensitive but also want consistent latency.
[00:01:47] Priya Shah: typical tradeoff: hosted gives fastest time to market and simpler auth, dedicated gives better tail latency and predictability. we usually propose starting hosted for 2-week validation then move to dedicated if steady throughput is needed. but if you have enterprise customers who require VPC or on-prem, we can run private with our private control plane.
[00:02:04] Eric Wong: that makes sense. most targets are mid-market, expecting SSO and audit logs.
[00:02:09] Jordan Lee: let's capture that as a gating condition — SSO (SAML/Okta) plus audit logs and encryption-at-rest via customer KMS for any enterprise pilot.

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, some speaker tags fuzzy):
[00:05:03] Jordan Lee: ok first account cluster — three targets: NovaRetail, MediQ Health, and FleetOps. Maya you flagged NovaRetail as top priority?
[00:05:11] Maya Patel: yes NovaRetail is first, they want live product recommendations and in-session personalization. low latency is important. they also need PCI-adjacent controls, not full scope but they want logs and token retention policies.
[00:05:26] Priya Shah: note — for recommendation models we recommend enabling prefix caching and a short KV cache window; that cuts token compute for repeated sessions. i'll include that in the bench config.
[00:05:37] Sofia Ramos: can you explain the KV cache bits again? sometimes our infra people say K V cash which is hilarious.
[00:05:44] Priya Shah: (laugh) yeah auto transcribes as K V cash — it's KV cache, it's basically keeping the key-value attention cache in memory to avoid recomputing earlier layers. helps for interactive sessions. it works best when session pattern has repeats.
[00:05:58] Eric Wong: i'd like to understand how that impacts cost — is that a big line item?
[00:06:02] Priya Shah: it reduces per-token GPU work so net cost per request usually drops, but it increases memory pressure. on dedicated pools you get more headroom, on hosted we manage eviction policies. we'll show numbers in the bench tab.

[00:09:12] Maya Patel: security checklist — SSO, SAML, SCIM, and audit logs; do you support customer-managed keys?
[00:09:20] Jordan Lee: yes, for Private deployments we integrate with KMS/HSM and provide an audit log feed. for Hosted we offer managed encryption and can ship audit logs to a secure S3 with retention controls. we'll need to confirm retention period with NovaRetail.
[00:09:35] Sofia Ramos: regarding SSO, is there an SP-initiated flow doc? our SRE will need it.
[00:09:41] Priya Shah: i'll drop the SSO runbook and sample metadata. note: there was a minor inconsistency earlier in the runbook where the service provider entity id used the old redwood domain — we'll update that.

[00:12:50] Jordan Lee: quick pipeline triage — NovaRetail is green if we provide pilot plan + pricing; MediQ needs an extra compliance review (HIPAA adjacent), might require Private. FleetOps is price-sensitive, likely hosted.
[00:13:06] Maya Patel: sounds right. does Redwood have an explicit HIPAA offering or BAA?
[00:13:12] Jordan Lee: we have HIPAA support options and partner checklists; legal signed BAA is possible for Private deployments — i'll note legal will need to review scope.

[00:15:30] Eric Wong: i want to understand co-sell motion economics — how do we present joint pricing? do you have partner SKUs?
[00:15:37] Jordan Lee: yes we have partner SKU mappings and suggested margins for GTM. typical structure is: list price for hosted api, discounted partner SKU for co-sell, and dedicated seat pricing for committed capacity. i'll send the spreadsheet with suggested discount tiers.
[00:15:52] Eric Wong: perfect. also which competitors do we lean on vs when talking to customers?
[00:15:57] Priya Shah: we usually position on production economics — cheaper at scale vs generalist APIs. Competitors we commonly see: Anthropic and OpenAI for conversational APIs, Cohere for embeddings, and infra players like KServe for self-hosted. emphasize our routing, caching, and fallback features.

[00:19:20] Sofia Ramos: technical pilot — what does a 2-week pilot look like? what metrics do we measure?
[00:19:26] Priya Shah: recommended pilot: week 1 smoke + small traffic test, week 2 ramp to production-like load. metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens per session, cost per 1k tokens, error rates, and model quality (via our eval harness on a prompt set you provide).
[00:19:42] Jordan Lee: add SLO on availability and a quality threshold — e.g., precision for recommendation use-case must be above X on your eval set. Sofia, if you can provide a 100 prompt eval set we can run the quality regression suite.
[00:19:55] Sofia Ramos: yes i'll pull 100 prompts and a small gold-set of expected outputs. question — do you support function calling and structured outputs?
[00:20:02] Priya Shah: yes streaming and function/tool call patterns are supported; we'll include an example payload. some older model variants expose slightly different tokens-per-call. we'll annotate those in the bench.

[00:23:40] Maya Patel: stakeholder alignment — field enablement materials? playbooks?
[00:23:44] Jordan Lee: we have a partner playbook template and a short field training deck. i'll share both plus a 30-minute enablement session recording.
[00:23:51] Eric Wong: would be great to co-brand the deck for customer-facing presentations.
[00:23:55] Jordan Lee: yes we can provide a cobranded deck asset.

[00:26:10] Sofia Ramos: networking — will there be IP allowlisting or VPC peering for dedicated?
[00:26:16] Priya Shah: for Dedicated we can do VPC peering and private subnet connectivity; for Private we do full VPC controls and on-prem options. hosted is public with IP allowlists as an option. we'll need to exchange CIDR ranges if you want peering.

[00:29:02] Maya Patel: contract and procurement — what's the typical timeline for getting a pilot contract out?
[00:29:07] Jordan Lee: if it's hosted pilot, we use a standard partner pilot addendum — usually 7-10 business days once SOW is agreed. for Private or Dedicated with enterprise terms, legal review might add 3-4 weeks.

[00:32:21] Eric Wong: potential blocker — some prospects are insisting on data residency in eu-west. does Redwood have region coverage?
[00:32:28] Jordan Lee: yes we have hosted regions in NA and EU, and Private can be deployed into EU region or on-prem. we'll confirm the region-specific audit log endpoints.

[00:35:40] Priya Shah: we also discussed fallback routing — if dedicated pool is saturated we can automatically route to a slightly quantized model to maintain availability. that's part of graceful degradation. note: quantization can change output tokens slightly — we'll surface those diffs in the quality report.

[00:38:10] Sofia Ramos: for FleetOps, which is price-sensitive, is there a way to lower token cost? e.g., smaller model or quantized variant?
[00:38:17] Priya Shah: yes, suggest smaller variant + 8-bit quantization. combine that with caching and batching to reduce cost. we'll run synthetic numbers for FleetOps pattern.

[00:41:00] Jordan Lee: ok action recap — Jordan will send pricing and partner SKU mapping, Priya will attach bench spreadsheets and SSO runbook, Sofia will provide the 100-prompt eval set and SSO requirements, Maya will pull pilot account list. we'll sync next Tuesday to lock the pilot plan.
[00:41:18] Maya Patel: confirmed.
[00:41:21] Eric Wong: timeline looks good.

Final Qs and loose threads:
[00:45:30] Sofia Ramos: for the bench runs, do you need real customer traffic or synthetic?
[00:45:35] Priya Shah: synthetic is fine for initial latency/cost numbers; we'll do a small sample of real traffic for quality checks if your customers agree.
[00:46:10] Maya Patel: do you have a list of required contract terms? procurement will want that.
[00:46:15] Jordan Lee: i'll include a checklist for procurement (BAA, DPA, data residency, SLA terms).

[00:49:00] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, great session. next call — technical pilot kickoff week of March 16th. we'll circulate invites.
[00:49:08] Maya Patel: thanks, talk soon.
[00:49:10] Eric Wong: thanks all.
[00:49:12] Sofia Ramos: bye.
